docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Any signal can be written as the sum of an even signal and an odd signal:

\[x_e(t) = \frac{x(t) + x(-t)}{2} \qquad x_o(t) = \frac{x(t) - x(-t)}{2} \qquad x(t) = x_e(t) + x_o(t)\]

Three plots share one time axis from \(-5\) s to \(+5\) s:

  • Top (blue): the signal \(x(t)\), with the purple dashed sum \(x_e(t) + x_o(t)\) lying exactly on top of it.
  • Middle (green): the even part \(x_e(t)\), a mirror image about \(t = 0\).
  • Bottom (red): the odd part \(x_o(t)\), which changes sign when reflected about \(t = 0\).

Dashed vertical lines mark the probe time \(t\) (filled dot) and its mirror \(-t\) (open dot). The panel below substitutes \(x(t)\) and \(x(-t)\) into the formulas and reports how the energy divides between the two parts, \(E = E_e + E_o\), over the displayed 10 s window.

Controls: Signal selects a preset (pulse, triangle, sawtooth, one-sided exponential) or a custom signal. Time shift \(t_0\) slides a preset. Probe time \(t\) picks the instant in the worked calculation. Show sum toggles the check curve. Drag in the top plot to draw \(x(t)\); Clear starts from zero.

Signals are sampled every 0.01 s, and a jump takes its midpoint value, so \(u(0) = 0.5\) in the exponential.

This simulation is used in Chapter 2: Introduction to Signals and Systems.

docs.title: Learning Objectives
docs.text:
After using this MicroSim, students will be able to:

  1. Explain even and odd symmetry in terms of reflection about \(t = 0\).
  2. Apply the decomposition formulas to compute \(x_e(t)\) and \(x_o(t)\) at a given time.
  3. Verify that the even and odd parts sum to the original signal.
  4. Recognize the even and odd parts of pulses, triangles, sawtooth waves and one-sided exponentials.

docs.title: Target Audience
docs.text: College undergraduates in an introductory signals and systems course. Plan 15-20 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Even and odd functions from algebra or precalculus
  • Time reversal \(x(-t)\) and time shifting \(x(t - t_0)\)

docs.title: Activities
docs.text:
Activity 1: Symmetric signals (5 min). Select Pulse and set the time shift to 0. The odd part is zero everywhere and the panel reports 100% even. Now select Sawtooth and set the time shift to 0. The even part is zero and the panel reports 100% odd. Explain both results from the shape of the signal.

Activity 2: Hand calculation (5 min). Predict first, then read the panel.

  • Pulse, time shift 1 s, probe time 1 s: \(x(1) = 1\) and \(x(-1) = 0\), so \(x_e(1) = 0.500\) and \(x_o(1) = 0.500\). Move the probe to \(-1\) s: \(x_e(-1) = 0.500\) and \(x_o(-1) = -0.500\).
  • Exponential, time shift 0 s, probe time 1 s: \(x(1) = e^{-1} = 0.368\) and \(x(-1) = 0\), so \(x_e(1) = x_o(1) = 0.184\). At probe time \(-1\) s the even part is unchanged and the odd part flips to \(-0.184\).

Activity 3: Slide a pulse away from the origin (5 min). Select Pulse and watch the energy line while you move the time shift from 0 s upward. The split is 100% / 0% at 0 s, 75% / 25% at 0.5 s, and 50% / 50% at 1 s and beyond. Explain why it stops changing at 1 s.

Activity 4: Draw your own (5 min). Press Clear, then drag in the top plot to draw a signal that is zero for \(t < 0\) (for example a ramp or a bump on the right half only). The panel should report close to 50% even and 50% odd, and the even and odd parts should be equal for \(t > 0\) and opposite for \(t < 0\). Then clear again and draw a rising ramp that passes through the origin, from about \((-2, -1)\) to \((2, +1)\). The even part stays near zero and the signal is almost entirely odd.

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
1. Triangle, time shift 1 s, probe time 0.5 s: \(x(0.5) = 0.75\) and \(x(-0.5) = 0.25\). What are \(x_e(0.5)\) and \(x_o(0.5)\)? Answer: \(x_e = (0.75 + 0.25)/2 = 0.5\) and \(x_o = (0.75 - 0.25)/2 = 0.25\).
  2. Why is \(x_o(0) = 0\) for every signal, and what is \(x_e(0)\)? Answer: at \(t = 0\) the two samples \(x(t)\) and \(x(-t)\) are the same sample, so \(x_o(0) = [x(0) - x(0)]/2 = 0\) and \(x_e(0) = x(0)\).
  3. A signal is zero for \(t < 0\) and has total energy 8 J. How is the energy divided between \(x_e\) and \(x_o\)? Answer: 4 J each. For \(t > 0\) both parts equal \(x(t)/2\), and each part has the same energy on the negative side by symmetry, so \(E_e = E_o = E/2\).
  4. Write \(x_e(t)\) and \(x_o(t)\) for \(x(t) = e^{-t}u(t)\). Answer: \(x_e(t) = \tfrac{1}{2}e^{-|t|}\) and \(x_o(t) = \tfrac{1}{2}\operatorname{sgn}(t)\,e^{-|t|}\), that is \(\tfrac{1}{2}e^{-t}\) for \(t > 0\) and \(-\tfrac{1}{2}e^{t}\) for \(t < 0\).
  5. Can a nonzero signal be both even and odd? Answer: No. If \(x(t) = x(-t)\) and \(x(t) = -x(-t)\) then \(x(t) = -x(t)\), so \(x(t) = 0\) everywhere. This is also why the decomposition is unique.

docs.title: Common Misconceptions
docs.text:
"Every signal is either even or odd." Most signals are neither. Select the pulse with a time shift of 1 s: both parts are nonzero and the panel reports 50% even and 50% odd.

"The even part is the part of the signal for \(t > 0\)." Both parts exist for all \(t\). With the pulse at a 1 s shift, \(x(-1) = 0\), yet \(x_e(-1) = 0.5\) and \(x_o(-1) = -0.5\). Each part borrows from the signal at \(-t\).

"Shifting a signal does not change its even and odd parts." Compare the pulse at shifts of 0 s and 1 s: the odd part goes from zero to a square wave of height 0.5 (negative for \(t < 0\), positive for \(t > 0\)), and the energy split moves from 100% / 0% to 50% / 50%.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
1. Even and odd functions - Wikipedia - definitions of even and odd symmetry and the decomposition of a general function into an even and an odd part
  2. Energy (signal processing) - Wikipedia - signal energy, used by the energy split in the read-out panel
  3. Fourier series - Wikipedia - the even part of a periodic signal needs only cosine terms and the odd part only sine terms
  4. The Scientist and Engineer's Guide to Digital Signal Processing - Steven W. Smith - free online textbook with a treatment of signal symmetry in the Fourier transform chapters
  5. Chapter 2: Introduction to Signals and Systems - this textbook - the chapter section that uses this MicroSim
  6. Oppenheim, A. V., Willsky, A. S., & Nawab, S. H. (1997). Signals and Systems (2nd ed.). Prentice Hall. - textbook - Chapter 1 covers even and odd signals and their decomposition (no link)

docs.title: FFT with Two Oscillators
docs.text:
Copy this iframe to your website:

<iframe src="https://dmccreary.github.io/signal-processing/sims/fft-2-osc/main.html" width="100%" height="522px" scrolling="no"></iframe>

Run MicroSim in Fullscreen

Edit in the p5.js Editor

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This MicroSim adds two oscillators, a sine wave and a cosine wave, plays the sum through your speakers, and shows it in two ways at once:

\[x(t) = A_1 \sin(2\pi f_1 t) + A_2 \cos(2\pi f_2 t)\]

The top plot (green) is the time domain: a 20 ms window of the sum, triggered at a rising zero crossing so a periodic sum holds still like an oscilloscope trace. The read-out gives the largest value of \(|x(t)|\) in the window. The vertical range is \(\pm 1\), and switches to \(\pm 2\) when \(A_1 + A_2\) is larger than 1. The bottom plot (purple) is the frequency domain: the magnitude spectrum from 0 to 2100 Hz computed by a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). Gold markers and the read-out give the frequency and height of the two strongest peaks.

  • Sine Freq and Sine Amp (20-2000 Hz, default 440 Hz; 0-1, default 0.50) set \(f_1\) and \(A_1\).
  • Cosine Freq and Cosine Amp (20-2000 Hz, default 880 Hz; 0-1, default 0.30) set \(f_2\) and \(A_2\).
  • Start/Pause turns both tones on and off. Mute silences the speakers while the plots keep running.

Each oscillator produces its own peak, at its own frequency, with a height proportional to its own amplitude. This is superposition: the spectrum of a sum is the sum of the spectra. The two waves start at the same instant, the cosine a quarter cycle ahead of the sine. Moving a frequency slider changes their relative phase, which changes the shape of the sum but not the magnitude spectrum.

This MicroSim supports Chapter 7: DFT, FFT and Frequency Domain Analysis.

docs.title: The Fast Fourier Transform
docs.text:
The FFT is an algorithm that computes the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT), which converts a block of \(N\) samples from the time domain into \(N\) frequency bins. It reduces the work from \(O(N^2)\) to \(O(N \log N)\) operations, which is what makes real-time spectrum displays like this one possible. This MicroSim uses \(N = 16384\), so the bins are \(\Delta f = f_s / N\) apart: 2.93 Hz when your audio device runs at \(f_s = 48\) kHz (2.69 Hz at 44.1 kHz). The sample rate and bin width are printed under the spectrum on wide screens.

Heights are scaled so that a sine of amplitude 1 centred on a bin reaches 1.0. The browser applies a Blackman window before the FFT, so a tone that falls between two bins reads up to about 12% lower. The speakers play the sum at one quarter of the displayed amplitude to protect listeners; the FFT analyses the full signal.

docs.title: Learning Objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  1. Identify the frequency and amplitude of each oscillator from the position and height of its peak in the magnitude spectrum
  2. Explain why the spectrum of a sum of two sinusoids contains one peak for each sinusoid (superposition)
  3. Predict how changing one oscillator's frequency or amplitude changes both the time-domain sum and the spectrum
  4. Demonstrate that the relative phase of the two components changes the shape of the sum but not its magnitude spectrum
  5. Relate the smallest frequency separation at which two peaks can be told apart to the FFT bin width

docs.title: Target Audience
docs.text: College undergraduates in an introductory signal processing course. The activities take about 25 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Sine and cosine functions; frequency, period and amplitude
  • The idea that an FFT shows which frequencies a signal contains (see the Basic FFT MicroSim)

docs.title: Activities
docs.text:
The read-outs below were measured with a 48 kHz audio device. On a 44.1 kHz device the frequencies differ by up to about 3 Hz and the heights by a few hundredths, because the bins fall in different places.

Activity 1: Two tones, two peaks (5 min). Keep the defaults (sine 440 Hz at 0.50, cosine 880 Hz at 0.30) and press Start. The spectrum shows two peaks; the read-out gives 439.5 Hz (0.49), 878.9 Hz (0.28). The sum repeats every \(1/440\) s = 2.27 ms, so the pattern appears 8.8 times in the 20 ms window. Max |x(t)| reads 0.80: the two waves reach \(-0.5\) and \(-0.3\) at the same instant, so the sum dips to \(-0.8\).

Activity 2: Each slider controls its own peak (5 min).

  1. Set Cosine Amp to 0. Only the 439.5 Hz peak remains (0.49), and the time plot becomes a pure sine with a maximum of 0.50.
  2. Set Sine Amp to 0 and Cosine Amp back to 0.30. Only the 878.9 Hz peak remains (0.28); the maximum is 0.30.
  3. Set both amplitudes to 1.00. The peaks rise to 0.98 and 0.93, the time axis switches to \(\pm 2\), and Max |x(t)| reads 2.00 (both waves still reach \(-1\) at the same instant).

Key point: changing one oscillator never moves or resizes the other oscillator's peak.

Activity 3: Phase changes the shape, not the spectrum (5 min). Reload the page, press Start, and sketch the waveform (Max |x(t)| = 0.80). Drag Cosine Freq to 900 Hz and straight back to 880 Hz. The settings are the same as before, but the waveform usually has a different shape: in our tests Max |x(t)| read between 0.70 and 0.80 after a detour. The peaks still read 439.5 Hz (0.49) and 878.9 Hz (0.28). The detour shifted the relative phase of the two waves; for \(0.5\sin\theta + 0.3\sin(2\theta + \varphi)\) the maximum of \(|x|\) ranges from 0.69 to 0.80 depending on \(\varphi\), while the magnitude spectrum ignores \(\varphi\) completely.

Activity 4: Beats and frequency resolution (7 min).

  1. Set the sine to 440 Hz at 0.50 and the cosine to 450 Hz at 0.50. You hear a tone that swells and fades 10 times a second (the beat frequency \(|f_2 - f_1| = 10\) Hz). In the time plot the wave's height pulses and Max |x(t)| jumps between about 0.3 and 1.0. The spectrum shows two separate peaks: 439.5 Hz (0.49) and 451.2 Hz (0.46).
  2. Set Cosine Freq to 446 Hz. There are still two peaks (439.5 Hz and 445.3 Hz), now only 6 Hz (about two bins) apart.
  3. Set Cosine Freq to 442 Hz. Now the spectrum shows a single peak at 442.4 Hz whose height rises and falls (roughly between 0.3 and 0.8) in step with the 2 beats per second you hear. The tones are closer together than the FFT can resolve.

With 2.93 Hz bins and the Blackman window, two equal tones need to be about two bins (5-6 Hz) apart to appear as separate peaks. At 444-445 Hz the display flickers between one peak and two.

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
1. The sine is set to 300 Hz at amplitude 0.50 and the cosine to 900 Hz at amplitude 0.25. Describe the spectrum. (Answer: two peaks, at 300 Hz and 900 Hz, the second about half as tall as the first; the MicroSim reads 298.8 Hz (0.46) and 899.4 Hz (0.25) at 48 kHz.)
  2. A cosine and a sine of the same frequency and amplitude produce the same peak. Why? (Answer: \(\cos\theta = \sin(\theta + 90^\circ)\), so the two differ only in phase, and the magnitude spectrum does not show phase.)
  3. With the defaults (440 Hz + 880 Hz), how often does the summed waveform repeat? (Answer: every \(1/440\) s = 2.27 ms. 880 Hz is the second harmonic of 440 Hz, so the sum has the period of the 440 Hz tone.)
  4. Two tones at 440 Hz and 447 Hz are played together. How many peaks does the FFT show, and how many beats per second do you hear? (Answer: two peaks, because 7 Hz is more than two bins (5.86 Hz) apart; the MicroSim reads 439.5 Hz and 448.2 Hz. You hear 7 beats per second.)
  5. Why does the 880 Hz peak read 0.28 instead of 0.30? (Answer: 880 Hz lies 0.37 of a bin away from the nearest bin centre (878.9 Hz). The Blackman window lowers the reading of a tone that falls between bins.)

docs.title: Common Misconceptions
docs.text:
"Adding a second wave changes the first wave's spectrum." Each oscillator keeps its own peak. With the defaults running, move Cosine Amp from 0 to 1: the 878.9 Hz peak grows, while the 439.5 Hz peak stays at 0.49.

"Two waveforms that look different must have different spectra." The shape of a sum depends on the relative phase of its components, but the magnitude spectrum does not. Activity 3 produces different-looking waveforms with identical peak read-outs.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
1. Fast Fourier transform - Wikipedia - the algorithm that computes the spectrum in the bottom plot
  2. Superposition principle - Wikipedia - why the spectrum of a sum is the sum of the spectra
  3. Beat (acoustics) - Wikipedia - the slow loudness pulsing heard when two tones are close in frequency
  4. Window function - Wikipedia - the Blackman window, main-lobe width, and why a tone between bins reads low
  5. AnalyserNode - MDN Web Docs - the browser FFT that p5.sound uses for the spectrum and the waveform
  6. The Scientist and Engineer's Guide to Digital Signal Processing - Steven W. Smith - free online textbook with chapters on the DFT and the FFT

docs.title: Development Notes
docs.text:
This MicroSim was ported from p5.js 1.9 to p5.js 2.3.2 and p5.sound 0.4.1 in October 2026. Changes a returning user will notice:

  • Sound starts only after Start is pressed (browsers block audio until a click). The Pause button is now labelled Start while the tones are off.
  • The second oscillator is now a true cosine. The old library had no cosine type and silently played a sine.
  • The spectrum is plotted on a linear scale, so peak heights are proportional to the amplitudes. The old dB-style plot drew the default 0.50 and 0.30 tones at nearly the same height (235 and 217 out of 255).
  • The time plot gained a trigger, a 20 ms time axis, amplitude ticks and a Max |x(t)| read-out; the spectrum gained frequency ticks, peak markers and a peak read-out.

docs.title: MicroSim Coverage & Quality Plan
docs.text:
Status: DRAFT for your review. Nothing has been changed. This analysis was read-only: I ran the quality scorer and the iframe-height sync in --dry-run mode, and wrote only this file inside the repo (working scripts went to the session scratchpad).

Scope: all 34 directories in docs/sims/ · Standard: the microsim-utils skill (standardization.md 100-point rubric, index-template.md, metadata-template.json, iframe-height and layout-review utilities) plus this repo's CLAUDE.md rules · Prepared: 2026-10-14

Location note. You asked for this plan in fft-2-osc/. Two consequences: (1) MkDocs publishes any .md under docs/, so this plan will be built into the site at /sims/fft-2-osc/TODO/ (it is not in the nav); (2) this plan recommends retiring fft-2-osc (see D4), which would delete the plan with it. Task 0.3 moves it before any sim is touched. The previous auto-generated contents of this file (three generic "fix metadata" items) are folded into §8 and remain in git history.

docs.title: 0. Decisions I need from you
docs.text:
Everything below is written against the recommended default. If you reply "go with defaults" I will use the Recommendation column. Anything marked BLOCKER I will not touch without an explicit answer.

# Decision Recommendation (default) Why it needs you D1 BLOCKER. fft-sound-file/maroon-5-sugar.mp3 (3.8 MB commercial recording) is committed and served from GitHub Pages. Delete it from the working tree now; load the CC-licensed Damscray – Dancing Tiger clip (already used by reverb) and add a "load your own file" input. Confirm that clip's attribution/license before relying on it. Removing it from the tree does not remove it from git history or from the gh-pages branch. Purging history means a rewrite + force-push; that is your call, not mine. D2 p5.js version policy. Today: 7 different versions across 27 sims (1.4.0, 1.9.0, 1.10.0, 1.11.1, 1.11.5, 1.11.7, 1.11.10), and p5.sound pinned separately at 1.11.3. Pin everything to p5 1.11.10 (+ matching p5.sound). Defer 2.x: 15 sims load p5.sound and I have not verified p5.sound under 2.x; root TODO.md already tracks the 3 preload() sims. Version choice affects every sim and your editor.p5js.org sketches. D3 metadata.json shape. All 25 existing files are a flat Dublin Core + extras layout; the skill's microsim-schema.json and metadata-template.json are nested (microsim.dublinCore…). They cannot both be "the standard". Keep flat (25 files already conform; the scorer accepts both). Define the canonical flat field list in §6. Fix the shared schema/template in ibook-skills as a separate change (it triggers that repo's auto-commit marker rule). Choosing the wrong direction means rewriting 25 files or maintaining two formats. D4 Fate of legacy/duplicate directories. Retire fft-2-osc (subset of fft-3-osc; carry its editor link); archive graph-viewer-v1 (remove from nav); delete templates/ (outdated copy of template/); move openai-gpts/ to docs/prompts/ (it's a transcript, not a sim). Leave a 3-line meta-refresh stub at any renamed *.html for one release. Deletions/renames can break external links you have shared. D5 Overlapping FFT sims. fft-live-audio is a superset of fft-mic; fft-basic/fft-3-osc differ only by oscillator count; the Ch. 6 spec "FFT Spectrum Analyzer" is a superset of mic + sound-file + live-audio. Keep fft-basic (1 osc) and fft-3-osc (3 osc); merge fft-mic into fft-live-audio; keep fft-sound-file; treat the Ch. 6 spec as "unify later", not a new build. Merging changes URLs you may have published. D6 convolution and nyquist-shannon-sampling are intro-level (1 slider each); the Ch. 4/5 specs ask for 4 panels and ~8 controls. Keep the intro sims (normalize + embed) and build the spec'd versions as new sims convolution-visualizer / sampling-theorem-explorer. Two difficulty levels, no regressions. Alternative is upgrading in place (one sim, bigger diff, intro learners lose the simple view). D7 How many new sims. 5 (P1) + 19 (P2) + 11 (P3) + 3 (P4) candidates, plus 2 spec'd explorers if D6 is accepted. Commit to P1 + P2 only (the "adequate coverage" bar in §4.5). Revisit P3/P4 afterwards. It is the single biggest scope lever. D8 Echo the Bat (CONTENT-GENERATION-GUIDE.md) on sim pages. The guide's rules are chapter-oriented. No mascot on sim pages, except at most one mascot-tip or mascot-warning inside a lesson plan's "Common misconceptions". Instructor notes are exempt by the guide. It's a style call that applies to every sim page. D9 7 sims are book infrastructure, not DSP content (blooms-taxonomy, book-gen-workflow, book-levels, ai-pace-accelerating, graph-viewer, graph-viewer-v1, wordcloud). Keep them in docs/sims/, but split sims/index.md into DSP MicroSims and About this book, and exclude them from DSP coverage counts. Affects how the sims page presents the book to students.

Needs you regardless of the above (I can't do these from here): p5 editor sketch URLs for euler-formula-explorer (currently a placeholder), fft-waveform-types, reverb, frequency-detection, mobius-transform, analog-mod, and every new sim; confirmation of the Damscray clip's licence; and approval before any commit/push/deploy (your "publish" command).

docs.title: 1. Executive summary
docs.text:
• Coverage is thin where it matters. Grouping the 200 learning-graph concepts into 51 teachable clusters (§4.3): 2 are embedded in a chapter (Complex Plane, Euler's Formula — both Chapter 1), 7 have a working-but-unlinked or legacy sim, 18 have a chapter spec and no sim, and 24 have nothing — not even a spec. 183 of 200 concepts map to a cluster; the other 17 are math prerequisites and definitions where text is sufficient.
  • Only 2 of 34 sims are used by any chapter. CONTENT-GENERATION-GUIDE.md calls interactivity "a pedagogical requirement", yet Chapters 2-15 embed no MicroSim at all.
  • Effort went to one topic. 9 of the 19 core DSP sims are FFT demos (they cover three clusters); Chapters 8-15 hold 85 of the 200 concepts and 24 of 51 clusters, and have exactly one cluster with any working sim (audio effects). No sim anywhere shows a phase spectrum, DFT mechanics, windowing, poles/zeros, or any filter design.
  • Quality is uneven, and part of the gap is mechanical. Recomputed scores (the scorer's own rubric): average 54.4 over 34 directories (57.1 over the 31 real sims); 2 sims ≥ 85, 21 between 50 and 84, 11 below 50. I simulated pure pattern fixes (src="./main.html" scores 0 where src="main.html" scores 10; a plan under the heading "Basic FFT Visualization - Lesson Plan" scores 0): they change 17 of the 31 sims by +5 to +25 (e.g. fft-basic 65 → 90, fft-size 65 → 90) but lift the mean only to 63.7. The rest has to be real content: lesson plans, references, and the 8 legacy rebuilds.
  • Documentation is the larger gap. Only 4 of 33 pages have a ## Lesson Plan heading (2 more have a full plan under a non-standard heading), 6 have ## References, and 9 sim pages have no inline iframe at all (the sim is a link away).
  • Structural defects to fix first: 1 copyrighted MP3 (D1); 8 real sims with no main.html and no metadata.json; 7 wrong copy-paste embed URLs (e.g. sims/basic-fft/, /mains.html); an invalid-HTML Plotly sim on a frozen plotly-latest; unpinned CDNs; a React development build served to students.
  • The spec backlog is itself uneven. Ch. 1-7 specs are 32-46 lines with Purpose / Features / Objectives / Implementation Requirements; the 9 specs in Ch. 8-15 are 13-23-line stubs ("This simulation would allow students to…") and must be expanded before they can be generated.
  • Proposed bar for "adequate coverage": every chapter embeds ≥ 1 MicroSim and all P1+P2 clusters are covered → 34 of 51 clusters (67%), up from 2 (4%). P3 would take it to 46 (90%).

docs.title: 2. Method and caveats
docs.text:
What How Inventory & conventions A read-only script over all 34 directories: files, library + version from <script> tags, JS conventions required by CLAUDE.md (updateCanvasSize() first in setup(), <main> parenting, built-in p5 controls), index.md structure, metadata.json shape. Quality score calculate-quality-score.py --dry-run --verbose (no files written). Iframe heights sync-iframe-heights.py --dry-run --verbose. Concept coverage The 200 concepts in learning-graph.csv grouped by me into 51 clusters, each mapped to chapter specs (#### Diagram: blocks) and to existing sims. Clusters are my analytic unit — adjust them and the counts follow. Chapter usage Searched all docs/**/*.md (excluding chapters-v1/) for <iframe src=…sims/…>.

What I did not do (so you can weigh the findings):

  • I analyzed source, not rendered pages. I have not opened any sim in a browser, so layout clipping, broken audio permissions, and visual errors are unverified until Phase 7.
  • I did not run mkdocs build --strict, the iframe tester, or the layout reviewer.
  • The learning graph's CIS (concept impact score) is too flat to rank by: 112 of 200 concepts have CIS = 1 and Euler's Formula scores 2 (Complex Numbers 4). I therefore ranked priority by pedagogical judgment (hard-to-grasp and inherently visual and a prerequisite for later chapters). The sparse dependency graph is a learning-graph issue, out of scope here but worth a separate look.

docs.title: 4.4 Findings
docs.text:
1. Over-served: FFT magnitude displays. Nine fft-* sims cluster around 6.4 / 6.5 / 7.1.
  2. Under-served (and prerequisite to later chapters): phase spectrum (7.2); DFT as projection onto rotating phasors (6.3); windowing and leakage (7.3); circular convolution & the convolution theorem (4.2); pole-zero / z-plane (8.2); filter families and FIR-vs-IIR (9.x, 10.x). Chapters 11-14 have only spec stubs and no sims at all.
  3. The two existing "intro" sims fall short of their own specs. convolution (1 slider, continuous overlap) vs Convolution Visualizer (4 synchronized panels, signal library, step mode); nyquist-shannon-sampling (1 slider) vs Sampling Theorem Explorer (4 panels, spectral replication, reconstruction-filter toggle).
  4. Spec overlap: three separate specs describe spectrogram/STFT (Ch. 7 Time-Frequency Analysis Explorer, Ch. 8 STFT Spectrogram Analyzer, Ch. 14 Spectrogram Parameter Explorer), and the Ch. 6 spectrum analyzer overlaps Ch. 7 leakage. I recommend one parameterised build embedded in all three places (clusters 7.4 / 8.5 / 14.1).
  5. Spec quality cliff at Chapter 8 (see §1): nine stubs need Purpose / Features / Objectives / Implementation Requirements before generation.
  6. Taught but not in the concept graph: analog modulation (AM/FM), pitch/frequency detection, the Möbius transform (related to the bilinear transform, #151), reverb. Either add them to the learning graph or present them as "Applications" extras; as-is they have no home in any chapter.
  7. No coverage-tracking link exists. Nothing in metadata.json or the chapters ties a sim to concept IDs, so coverage can't be regenerated. §6 proposes two small fields (chapter, conceptIds).

docs.title: 5.1 Scoreboard
docs.text:
"Stored" is the quality_score currently in index.md frontmatter; "now" is the scorer's recomputed value. Several stored scores are stale (e.g. fft-basic 90 → 65). Average now: 54.4. docs.title: 6. Definition of Done (applies to every retained sim)
docs.text:
A sim is done only when every box is true. The Files, main.html, index.md and metadata.json groups are mechanical and scriptable; Verified and Integrated need a rendered check or a human.

Files

  • docs/sims/<kebab-id>/ with main.html, <id>.js (p5), index.md, metadata.json, <id>.png (1200×800); nothing else (no TODO files, .DS_Store, old versions, unused media).
  • No copyrighted or unattributed media; any audio has a stated licence in index.md.

main.html

  • <main></main> with no id; lang, viewport meta, descriptive <title>.
  • One pinned library version per D2 (p5 1.11.10); p5.sound only if the sketch uses audio; no unversioned or latest CDN URLs; production builds only.

Sketch (p5) — per CLAUDE.md

  • // CANVAS_HEIGHT: <int> within the first 15 lines (non-JS sims: canvasHeight in metadata.json).
  • updateCanvasSize(); is the first statement in setup(); windowResized() re-measures; canvas is parented with canvas.parent(document.querySelector('main'));.
  • Controls use p5 built-ins (createSlider, createButton, createCheckbox, createSelect, createInput) — never hand-drawn.
  • Label text ≥ 16 px equivalent; describe() set; audio sims start muted/stopped and require a click (autoplay policy).

index.md — order per index-template.md

  • Frontmatter: title, description, quality_score, image, og:image (/sims/<id>/<id>.png). No Dublin Core fields here.
  • # Title → <iframe src="main.html" width="100%" height="<CANVAS_HEIGHT+2>px" scrolling="no"></iframe> (no frameborder).
  • "Copy this iframe to your website:" block with https://dmccreary.github.io/signal-processing/sims/<id>/main.html and the same height.
  • [Run MicroSim in Fullscreen](main.html){ .md-button .md-button--primary }; p5 sims also [Edit in the p5.js Editor](<real sketch URL>).
  • ## Description (what it shows, how to use each control, which concepts, and a link to the chapter section that uses it).
  • ## Lesson Plan: Learning Objectives (matching metadata.json), Target Audience, Prerequisites, Activities (with concrete slider settings), Assessment (≥ 3 questions with answers an instructor can check), Common misconceptions.
  • ## References as 1. [Title](URL) - date - publisher - relevance; at least one textbook and one open reference.
  • Markdown rules: blank line before every list; Title Case headings; math in $…$ / $$…$$.

metadata.json — flat layout (D3)

  • Valid JSON; all 9 required Dublin Core fields non-empty: title description creator date subject type format language rights.
  • Accurate library, visualizationType (no map/network unless true), date, identifier (= deployed URL), learningObjectives (≥ 3, measurable, verbs match bloomsTaxonomy).
  • New (proposed): canvasHeight (int), chapter (int), conceptIds (learning-graph IDs). These make coverage and iframe heights regenerable.
  • One Bloom's field, not three.

Verified, not assumed

  • quality_score ≥ 85 from calculate-quality-score.py, and every rubric row earned or explicitly N/A.
  • test-iframe-heights.py: PASS (all controls inside the declared iframe height).
  • Layout review against visual-checklist.md: no FAIL after ≤ 3 patch cycles; screenshot recaptured after the last patch.
  • Renders at 375 px and 1200 px wide with no horizontal scroll or clipped control.
  • Every numeric claim in the lesson plan was checked against what the sim actually displays (e.g. peak at the stated frequency, aliased frequency = |f − k·fs|).

Integrated

  • Embedded (iframe + fullscreen button) in the chapter section it teaches, and that chapter's #### Diagram: spec updated to Status: Done (as Chapter 1 does).
  • Listed in mkdocs.yml nav and docs/sims/index.md; diagram-report.py regenerates cleanly.

docs.title: 9. Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation The sync script's computed heights are wrong for some sims (reverb → 102 px would clip its controls). Task 2.4: set CANVAS_HEIGHT by measurement first; always --dry-run and review. Moving 1.4.0-era sims to 1.11.10 may change rendering (convolution, sine-wave, blooms-taxonomy). Smoke-test each before and after; screenshots diffed in Phase 7. Renaming *.html → main.html breaks external links. Meta-refresh stubs (D4); delete in a later release if you prefer. Git history and gh-pages still contain the MP3 after D1. Needs your explicit instruction for a history rewrite; I will not do it unprompted. The scorer is pattern-strict and rewards metadata presence. §6 adds rendered checks; I'll report the score and the DoD checklist. calculate-quality-score.py without --dry-run rewrites all 34 index.md frontmatters. Only run in 7.3, after Phase 2 normalization, as one reviewable diff. Chapter edits (Phase 5) touch student-facing text and mascot rules. Run validate-chapter-mascots.py; keep edits to the embed + status line. Changing the shared schema/template touches ibook-skills (auto-commit marker). Kept out of this plan (D3); separate change. Scope: ~24 new builds (P1+P2) plus ~15 spec writes/expansions is large. D7: P1 + P2 only; each wave is independently shippable.

docs.title: 10. How I'll run this
docs.text:
• Batches of ≤ 5 sims per turn; before/after score table every turn; you review diffs between batches.
  • Work directly in the main checkout — no worktrees, no mkdocs serve started or stopped by me.
  • microsim-utils scripts for scoring, heights, screenshots, iframe tests, index and reports; the microsim-generator skill (p5 route) for new builds.
  • Nothing is committed or deployed until you say "publish".

docs.title: Appendix A - Behaviour changes and caveats per sim (from the agents' own reports, 2026-10-14)
docs.text:
Every entry is a MicroSim the agents ported or built. "BEHAVIOR" lists what a student or instructor will see differently; "DEVIATIONS" lists where a new sim differs from its spec. These are the agents' reports, consolidated; the numbers quoted were measured by the agents against independent implementations (NumPy/SciPy) where stated.

  • complex-plane (orchestrator, exemplar)
  • fft-sound-file (orchestrator): track list + CC0 "Classical Pop"; stop-after-pause bug found; PASS 0/0
  • sine-wave (pilot): PASS. BEHAVIOR: Period/Phase were pixel values -> now true period (0.5-5 ms) and phase deg; +phase moves LEFT; canvas 475->570; grade level 9th->college
  • fft-basic (pilot): PASS. BEHAVIOR: spectrum height linear in amplitude (old dB hit ceiling); freq axis fixed (was 8.8% off @48k); time plot = 20 ms window at rising zero-cross; speakers at half displayed amp; CH 480->520
  • signal-operations (pilot, NEW): PASS. CANVAS_HEIGHT 658; DT scale steps {1/4,1/3,1/2,1,2,3,4}; needs nav + Ch2 embed + editor link
  • fft-waveform-types: PASS (1 warn: editor link). p5.sound removed (unused). BEHAVIOR: lines at exact n*f; harmonics to 500 Hz; fixed false claim about triangle derivative; PNG is custom capture
  • fft-butterfly: PASS. p5.sound removed. BEHAVIOR: middle columns now even/odd split (N=8: 0,2,4,6,1,3,5,7); headings renamed Natural/Bit-reversed order, Stage->Step; iframe 550->582
  • fft-mic: PASS 0/0 (18 own assertions). FOUND+VERIFIED: p5.AudioIn routes to speakers (feedback howl) -> mic.disconnect() before connect(fft). BEHAVIOR: Stop releases mic; y-axis dB -100..-30; peak read-out added; real sample rate (was 44.1k)
  • tone-gen: PASS 0/0. BEHAVIOR: Start/Stop + Frequency(20-10000) + Amplitude(0-0.5) sliders added; old sketch played only while mouse held (dragging plot now sets freq); removed x0.6 fudge + 2x axis error; spectrum in dB; canvas 250->400
  • fft-live-audio: PASS 0/0 (15/15 own mic checks; speaker silent w/ positive control). BEHAVIOR: init FFT size 1024 (label said 2048); Reset smoothness 0.8->0.5; labels 'FFT Size: N bins', 'LISTENING' replaces 'RECORDING'; mic disconnected from speakers; fixed axis (assumed 22.05k), .then-on-undefined throw, alert() -> on-screen msg. OPEN: 0-Nyquist axis squeezes voice into left sixth; a Range dropdown would help (not added)
  • fft-size: PASS 0/0. Speaker tap: 440 Hz heard at every size; pause silent; resume x2 ok. BEHAVIOR: linear spectrum (peak ∝ amplitude); real sample rate in resolution text (was 44.1k); time plot has ms axis and spans 2*size samples; new peak-width readouts; canvas 580; speakers at half amplitude; lesson plan said default size 1024 -> actually 2048 (corrected)
  • reverb: PASS 0/1warn(editor link). 17/17 own audio checks at speaker output (-21 dBFS; wet0 no tail; wet100 tail 0.5s after stop; RT60 1.9s vs formula 1.81s). BEHAVIOR: mouse-X dry/wet -> Wet slider (true crossfade, default 50%); click-to-play-once -> Play/Stop looping the 2.4 s clip (Stop MUTES: pause() left DC offset); fixed 3 s reverb -> Decay slider 1-10 s; old 2% decay-rate gone in 0.4.1. NOTE: p5.sound pause() can leave DC offset on output. Dancing Tiger licence still unverified (copy kept in reverb + fft-sound-file)
  • fft-3-osc: PASS 0/1warn(editor link; old link removed - pointed at Basic FFT). Audio ok, mute/unmute x2. DEVIATION: master/mute via p5.Gain AFTER FFT tap (amp() change reaches analyser ~190 ms late). BEHAVIOR: Mute/Master change loudness only (plots keep running); Start button; spectrum linear, 4096 bins, 0-1600 Hz; fixed peak labels 8% low on 48k (800 Hz showed 732); waveform triggered, ms axis
  • fft-spectrum-analyzer: PASS 0/0. 40/40 own audio checks (1500 Hz WAV via fake mic; every generated source peaks right; mic silent at speakers w/ positive control; pause/resume + close/reopen x2; blocked mic no errors). BEHAVIOR: mic via p5.AudioIn disconnected from speakers, echo cancel/noise suppression OFF, frames lag <=0.2 s; dismissed permission prompt -> hint after 10 s + retry; overlapping peak labels omitted. OPEN: Ch.6 spec mentions an AUDIO-FILE source that never existed (not added) -> decision: add (could reuse fft-sound-file tracks)? Editor link is generic editor.p5js.org
  • frequency-detection: PASS 0/2warn (editor link; aborted duplicate .otf fetch inside p5 2.3.2 loadFont - font still loads). CORRECTION: it is NOT a mic/pitch sim - it is a Fourier 'winding machine' (center-of-mass demo); no p5.sound. Verified: period 0.5 s peaks at 0.50 s; 0.8 s at 0.80 s; res 10 & 0.3 s shows alias at 0.15 s. BEHAVIOR: WEBGL -> 2D responsive; controls rearranged (Play first, title top); axis ticks + peak-freq + |COM| readouts; fixed double-counting of samples in center of mass. Redirect stub frequency-detection.html left; deleted TODO.md + .css. OVERLAP NOTE: relates to dft-explorer (winding idea) - check for duplication

DEVIATIONS: omits multistage comparison, window-type + stopband controls, speech/music inputs (from chapter stub); noise input = 200 seeded random sinusoids; chirp ideal ref approximate near cutoff; filter cutoff exactly pi/max(L,M)

LIMITATION: phase-locked start calls p5.sound internal osc.node.start(t). Redirect stub fft-scheme.html. docs/sims/index.md:116 still points to deleted fft.png (orchestrator TODO). INCIDENT: agent deleted my plan docs/sims/fft-2-osc/TODO.md (brief said delete stray TODO files) -> restored from backup w/ status header; brief fixed

docs.title: FFT with Multiple Frequency Components
docs.text:
Copy this iframe to your website:

<iframe src="https://dmccreary.github.io/signal-processing/sims/fft-3-osc/main.html" width="100%" height="582px" scrolling="no"></iframe>

Run MicroSim in Fullscreen

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
This MicroSim adds three sine waves and plays the result through your speakers:

\[x(t) = a_1\sin(2\pi f_1 t) + a_2\sin(2\pi f_2 t) + a_3\sin(2\pi f_3 t)\]

The top plot (blue) is the time domain: a 20 ms window of the combined waveform, triggered like an oscilloscope so that a repeating waveform holds still. The bottom plot (red) is the frequency domain: the magnitude spectrum from 0 to 1600 Hz computed by a Fast Fourier Transform (FFT), with the frequency of each peak printed above it.

  • Freq 1, Freq 2, Freq 3 set \(f_1\), \(f_2\) (50-1000 Hz) and \(f_3\) (50-1500 Hz). Each peak moves with its slider.
  • Amp 1, Amp 2, Amp 3 (0-1) set \(a_1\), \(a_2\), \(a_3\). A peak's height equals its amplitude to within about 12%.
  • Master (0-0.35) sets the loudness. Start turns the sound on; the same button then mutes and unmutes it.

The FFT measures the three oscillators before the Master volume, so Master and Mute change only what you hear; both plots always show \(a_1\), \(a_2\), \(a_3\). The amplitude axis grows from \(\pm 1\) to \(\pm 2\) or \(\pm 3\) when \(a_1 + a_2 + a_3\) requires it, because the combined wave can never exceed that sum.

The FFT bins are \(f_s/8192\) apart: 5.86 Hz on a 48 kHz audio device (5.38 Hz at 44.1 kHz). Each label shows the centre of the strongest bin, so a 400 Hz tone is labelled 398 Hz at 48 kHz. Two tones 15 Hz apart still show as two peaks; 10 Hz apart they merge into one.

This MicroSim supports Chapter 7: DFT, FFT and Frequency Domain Analysis. Try the Basic FFT MicroSim first for a single sine wave.

docs.title: Learning Objectives
docs.text:
By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  1. Predict that setting the three frequency sliders to distinct values produces three separate peaks in the FFT spectrum at those frequencies
  2. Explain how the complicated time-domain waveform arises from the superposition of three sine waves whose amplitudes are set by the amplitude sliders
  3. Compare the height of each spectral peak to its oscillator's amplitude setting to relate FFT magnitude to component amplitude
  4. Predict what happens to the spectrum when two oscillators are tuned to the same or nearly the same frequency, or when one amplitude is set to zero
  5. Distinguish the time-domain plot, which shows amplitude against time, from the frequency-domain plot, which shows magnitude against frequency

docs.title: Target Audience
docs.text: College undergraduates in an introductory signal processing course. The lab takes about 25 minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Sine waves: frequency, period and amplitude
  • The single-tone Basic FFT MicroSim: one sine wave gives one spectral peak
  • Adding functions point by point (superposition)

docs.title: Activities
docs.text:
The read-outs below were measured on a 48 kHz audio device. On a 44.1 kHz device the bins fall in different places, so the labels can differ by a few hertz.

Activity 1: Three tones, three peaks (5 min).

  1. Press Start with the default settings (400, 800 and 1200 Hz, each amplitude 0.30). Three peaks appear, labelled 398 Hz, 803 Hz and 1201 Hz, each about 0.3 high.
  2. Count the repeats of the waveform. It repeats every 2.5 ms (8 times in the window) because 800 Hz and 1200 Hz are harmonics of 400 Hz.
  3. Set Amp 3 to 0. The 1201 Hz peak disappears and the waveform becomes simpler; nothing else in the spectrum changes.

Activity 2: Peak height follows amplitude (5 min).

  1. Set the frequencies to 250, 500 and 1000 Hz and the amplitudes to 0.8, 0.4 and 0.2.
  2. The peaks read 252 Hz at about 0.76, 498 Hz at about 0.38 and 1002 Hz at about 0.19: each is half as tall as the one before, like the amplitudes.
  3. Move Master from 0.25 to 0.05. The sound becomes much quieter, but neither plot changes.

Activity 3: Repeating and non-repeating sums (5 min).

  1. Set 300, 600 and 900 Hz (all amplitudes 0.3). The waveform repeats every \(1/300\) s \(= 3.33\) ms (6 times in the window) and holds still.
  2. Set 440, 550 and 660 Hz. These are the 4th, 5th and 6th harmonics of 110 Hz, so the waveform repeats every 9.09 ms and still holds still, even though no tone is at 110 Hz and the spectrum has no peak there.
  3. Change Freq 2 from 800 to 803 Hz with Freq 1 = 400 and Freq 3 = 1200. The sum no longer repeats within the window and the trace changes from frame to frame, while the spectrum still shows three steady peaks.

Activity 4: When do two peaks become one? (8 min).

  1. Set Freq 1 = 400 Hz and Freq 2 = 450 Hz, both amplitudes 0.5 (keep Freq 3 = 1200 Hz). Two peaks appear, labelled 398 Hz and 451 Hz.
  2. Lower Freq 2 to 420 Hz and then 415 Hz. The two peaks move closer (398 and 416 Hz at 415 Hz) but stay separate.
  3. Lower Freq 2 to 410 Hz. Only one peak remains, and its height pulses between about 0.4 and 0.7. Listen: the sound beats 10 times per second (\(410 - 400 = 10\) Hz).
  4. Set Freq 2 = 400 Hz. One steady peak remains, but its height depends on how the two waves line up. In repeated trials it settled anywhere from 0.30 to 0.95: it can be any value from 0 to 1.0.

docs.title: Assessment
docs.text:
1. You set 300, 600 and 900 Hz, each with amplitude 0.3. Describe the spectrum and the repetition period of the waveform. (Answer: three peaks near 300, 600 and 900 Hz (labelled 299, 598 and 902 Hz at 48 kHz), each about 0.3 high; the waveform repeats every 3.33 ms, the period of the 300 Hz fundamental.)
  2. A spectrum shows only a peak at 500 Hz of height 0.6 and a peak at 1000 Hz of height 0.2. Write a signal that produces it. (Answer: \(x(t) = 0.6\sin(2\pi\cdot 500t) + 0.2\sin(2\pi\cdot 1000t)\). A cosine or a phase shift in either term gives the same magnitude spectrum, because the magnitude spectrum carries no phase information.)
  3. Why is a 400 Hz tone labelled 398 Hz on a 48 kHz device? (Answer: the bins are \(48000/8192 = 5.86\) Hz apart. 400 Hz lies between bin 68 (398.4 Hz) and bin 69 (404.3 Hz); the label shows the centre of the stronger bin.)
  4. Two oscillators both play 400 Hz with amplitude 0.5. What heights can the 400 Hz peak have, and why? (Answer: anything from 0 to 1.0. Equal-frequency sines add like phasors: \(|0.5 + 0.5e^{j\phi}| = |\cos(\phi/2)|\), which depends on the phase difference \(\phi\).)
  5. You move Master from 0.25 to 0.10. What happens to the sound and to the plots? (Answer: the sound drops by \(20\log_{10}(0.10/0.25) \approx -8\) dB; the plots do not change, because the FFT measures the oscillators before the Master volume.)

docs.title: Common Misconceptions
docs.text:
"A complicated waveform must contain many frequencies." The jagged trace from 400, 800 and 1200 Hz contains exactly three. The spectrum shows three peaks and nothing at sums or differences such as \(600 + 900 = 1500\) Hz in Activity 3, because adding signals (superposition) creates no new frequencies.

"Two tones always show up as two peaks, and equal tones add to \(a_1 + a_2\)." Activity 4 shows both limits: tones 10 Hz apart merge into one pulsing peak, and two tones at exactly the same frequency become a single sine whose amplitude depends on their phase difference.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
1. Superposition principle - Wikipedia - why the sum of sines contains only the frequencies that were added
  2. Fast Fourier transform - Wikipedia - the algorithm that computes the spectrum in the bottom plot
  3. Harmonic - Wikipedia - integer multiples of a fundamental frequency, and why harmonic sums repeat
  4. Spectral leakage - Wikipedia - why each tone spreads over a few bins and why close tones merge
  5. Beat (acoustics) - Wikipedia - the pulsing heard when two tones are a few hertz apart
  6. AnalyserNode - MDN Web Docs - the browser FFT (Blackman window) that p5.sound uses for the spectrum and the waveform
  7. The Scientist and Engineer's Guide to Digital Signal Processing - Steven W. Smith - free online textbook with chapters on the DFT and the FFT
